candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator and rewrite fraction parts as equivalent fractions before subtraction when denominators differ.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts use essentially identical names and definitions for creating equivalent fractions to match denominators before subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or a mixed number with an improper fractional part into a subtraction-ready form with standard whole and fractional parts.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and C each combine two preprocessing actions: rewriting whole numbers as mixed numbers with 0 fractional parts and normalizing improper mixed numbers. B isolates only the improper-mixed-number portion in S05; this is the closest match and reflects partial granularity mismatch.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions with like denominators and/or subtract the whole-number and fractional parts once the quantities are in compatible form.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and C each use one broader skill covering subtraction of like-denominator fractions and subtraction of separated whole/fraction parts in mixed numbers. B splits this into S02 for aligned fraction subtraction and S03 for subtracting mixed-number parts separately, so both map to the same broader cognitive concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units of the denominator when the fractional part of the minuend is too small to complete the subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the same regrouping/borrowing operation in mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the resulting fraction or mixed number to lowest terms, including recognizing when the result simplifies to a whole number or zero.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include the same post-subtraction simplification concept; B names it 'Simplify final result' but the operation is equivalent.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Combine the computed whole-number part and fractional part into the final mixed number, fraction, integer, or zero.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and C both distinguish recombining previously computed parts into a final expression as a separate step. B appears to absorb this into its broader mixed-part subtraction skill rather than coding it separately.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks align strongly on the core subtraction workflow: common denominators, subtraction, borrowing, and simplification. The main differences are granularity choices: Expert B splits subtraction into two skills and isolates improper mixed-number normalization, while Experts A and C use broader combined skills. Experts A and C also include a separate final recombination skill that Expert B does not represent independently. Every skill_id from all three experts has been mapped exactly once.
